Note::NlpAccessor::remove_emails¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::remove_emails() const

Delete Address-Shaped Email Tokens¶

remove_emails() deletes email-address spans while retaining the prose around them. It is appropriate when an address is incidental or sensitive and its presence does not need a replacement marker. Use mask_emails() when the downstream text should still record that an email occurred.

Recognition is deliberately lexical rather than a complete mail standard:

Component

Accepted bytes

Local part

ASCII letters, digits, ., _, %, +, and -

Separator

One @

Domain body

ASCII letters, digits, ., and -

Final suffix

A dot followed by at least two ASCII letters

This covers common tagged local parts and multi-label domains, including a+b@example.co.uk. It does not validate mailbox delivery, prohibit every structurally dubious dot placement, support quoted local parts, or recognize an address without a letter-only final suffix. In particular, a@b, @handle, and x@@example.com are left alone.

When a span is removed, remaining ASCII whitespace is collapsed and stripped. Punctuation adjacent to the address remains. If no valid span is found, the cell is returned byte-for-byte, including newlines and edge spaces. A cell consisting only of an address becomes an empty text cell, not an absent cell.

The method returns a new shape-identical Text Note and never mutates the receiver. It scans cells independently, uses an @ precheck to avoid regex work on impossible cells, propagates undefined, preserves empty shapes, and rejects Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes.

Example 1: Tagged And Multi-Label Addresses¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({
        "Write a+b@example.co.uk or x.y@sub.example.io today"})
        .nlp().remove_emails()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Write or today"]

Example 2: Invalid And Non-Email @ Forms Are Exact No-Ops¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({
        "  keep a@b, @handle, and x@@example.com\nexactly  "})
        .nlp().remove_emails()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["  keep a@b, @handle, and x@@example.com\nexactly  "]

Example 3: Complete Removal Preserves Matrix Shape¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a@b.io", "Page 1", "#tag", "<b>bold</b>"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix.nlp().remove_emails()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["", "Page 1"], 
  ["#tag", "<b>bold</b>"]
]

See Also¶

  • mask_emails: replace each recognized address with [EMAIL].

  • remove_urls: delete scheme or www. web links.

  • mask_pii: preserve several sensitive categories as named markers.
